pass_a_gloss: Reigns Lord into the age and into the age of-the age; you-will-perish, nations, from the land of-him; the desire of-the poor heard Lord. For it-is-necessary the Lord to-reign through the ages, until the desire of-the poor heard Lord, until he-put all the enemies a-footstool of-the feet of-him. For the kingdom of-him is the contemplation of-all the having-come-to-be and going-to-come-to-be ages; through which contemplation also the enemies friends become; and the land of-the Lord, the contemplation of-the having-come-to-be ages; and the kingdom, we-say, this: then he-hearkens-to the desire the Lord, whenever he-may-grant the desired-thing to-the having-desired soul.
pass_b_english: “The Lord reigns forever and to the age of the age; you nations shall perish from his land. The Lord heard the desire of the poor” (Psalm 9:37-38).
For the Lord must reign through the ages, until the Lord heard the desire of the poor, until he put all the enemies as a footstool of his feet (1 Corinthians 15:25).

For his kingdom is the contemplation of all the ages that have come to be and that will come to be; through which contemplation the enemies also become friends. And the land of the Lord is the contemplation of the ages that have come to be. And the kingdom, we say, is this: the Lord then hearkens to the desire, whenever he grants the desired thing to the soul that has desired.

choices.why: ἀπόλλυμι future middle 2pl + ἔθνη. Not ἀπολύω ‘release’ or ‘be silent’.
Standard ἄχρις οὗ. OCR α χρις ου is not Χριστός or χρῆν.
1 Corinthians 15:25 / Psalm 109:1 wording. Not merely ‘beneath his feet’.
Origen’s θεωρία of the ages, not ‘theory’ or a truncated hearing-clause.
